lines: +# What I trained on and why
+## Diagnosis (from `/opt/task/data/tb21_diagnostics`)
+On the 60-task TB2.1 eval set the base 4B (k=4 diagnostics) had 30 tasks at 0/4, 12 at 1/4, and 5 at 4/4.
+Most failures end in `Submitted` with partially-passing tests (plausible-but-wrong solutions, weak self-verification),
+not format collapse. Failures also run ~2x longer than passes (median 71 vs 38 steps; ~2x output tokens/step),
+so efficiency and stopping/verifying well looked like the main trainable gaps.
+## Training data (`/app/selection.jsonl`, 642 pool tasks, none modified)
+Static screen of all 7,234 pool tasks (instruction length, test count, oracle `solve.sh` length, task/verifier
+timeouts, Dockerfile size). Kept tasks that fit the training harness (600 s episode wall, 49k tokens) and match
+TB2.1 skill mix:
+- 520 TMax `short`/`moderate` (all TMax tasks are built for 600 s agent / 120 s verifier), 2-6 tests.
+- 122 SETA `medium`/`easy` with agent timeout <= 900 s (or expert estimate <= 15 min), verifier <= 900 s,
+  oracle solution 12-220 lines, weights summing to 1.0.
+Moderate/medium tasks got weight 2 (sampled twice as often). No pool task was repaired; manifest records 0 modified.
+## Run (`run1`, exported checkpoint = step 10)
+GRPO, 8 tasks x 8 episodes/step, temperature 1.0, max_seq_len 49152. lr 2e-6 for steps 0-6, then 3e-6 (live change).
+Trained 45 steps (~12 min/step; train-pool reward ~0.3-0.4, ~35% of GRPO groups informative), then stopped the run
+to evaluate checkpoints on TB2.1 (k=2, seed 0, cut episodes counted as failures):
+| checkpoint | TB2.1 pass@1 (k=2) |
+| step 20 (iter_19) | 0.042 (eval stopped early; clearly poor) |
+Longer training hurt TB2.1 badly: late checkpoints submit earlier with malformed/multi-block replies
+(format-error endings ~10% vs ~4% for base) — the short-horizon pool tasks reward finishing fast, which
+transfers poorly to long TB2.1 tasks. I therefore exported the best measured checkpoint, **step 10**,
+to `/app/checkpoint/`. Honest bottom line: at k=2/seed 0 it measures 0.225, still below the 0.263 base
+reference from the older k=4 measurement (different harness version, not directly comparable); with more
+time I would use a much lower LR, longer-horizon tasks, and evaluate every few steps.
